engine_memory_measured.question: how much memory does the engine actually need on NC inputs? The 4.1 GiB figure in circulation was measured on NEW_S inputs and nobody had measured these.
engine_memory_measured.CORRECTION_02_0xZ: The first reading of this receipt (mine, relayed to lead and to the integrator) called the 4.04 GiB drop in /dev/shm free space the PEAK memory of the engine and said it would be returned once the engine exited. That is wrong. Measured after the engine exited: free is still 2.31 GiB, and runs/ holds 4.1 GiB of engine OUTPUT FILES. The drop is a PERMANENT footprint, not a transient peak. Two different quantities were conflated: output files on a tmpfs, and transient anonymous memory.

shm_permanent_footprint_gib.note: runs/ is engine output and stays until deleted; exiting the engine does not reclaim it

transient_vs_permanent.transient_memory: cgroup anon peak 12.75 GiB is the transient figure, but the cgroup is SHARED with the other agents, so it is not attributable to this chain alone
transient_vs_permanent.the_4.1_GiB_NEW_S_figure: which of the two quantities it meant is not established, so comparing my 4.04 GiB against it was not like-for-like; that comparison is withdrawn

engine_memory_measured.hardlink_note: du on my root alone reports 7.6 GiB, while a du across /dev/shm/* reports 4.8 GiB for it, because work/NEWS_FEATURES.npz (2.8 GiB) is a HARDLINK shared with the nc root and is counted once per du invocation. The unique footprint is the smaller number.
